name: Typed Tool Boundary + Stateful Disclosure Budget
status: Prototype design with offline log replay; not yet a production benchmark

finding.title: Cumulative disclosure bypasses per-call controls
finding.summary: Individually capped or apparently allowed tool calls can be composed across turns into a bulk export. The local Qwen run produced 70 source-checked fictional patient rows across eight leaking turns; DeepSeek separately demonstrated full OFFSET pagination of 111 public-reference rows.
finding.novelty: The security failure is the sequence of tool actions, not one magic jailbreak string. A stateless row cap cannot express a session-level disclosure limit.
finding.scope: Patient disclosure is verified on the unofficial local Qwen target. The reviewed official DeepSeek and Claude runs did not verify patient PII extraction.

attackChain: Attacker frames each request as a small legitimate-looking lookup
The model emits a database tool call within the per-call row cap
Sensitive rows leave the tool boundary
Ranges or OFFSET advance across later turns
The attacker reconstructs a bulk dataset from individually bounded responses

control.placement: Between the agent and every tool, before execution, with a second check before output release
rules: Replace free-form SQL with typed operations: resource, approved fields, filters and limit.
Authorize resource and field combinations from role/purpose policy; the public Riley role cannot access patient or staff resources.
Track tainted entities and disclosed fields per session so repeated allowed calls cannot exceed a cumulative disclosure budget.
Canonicalize transformed output and apply deterministic taint/DLP checks before release.
Log the policy decision, rule ID, session and tool arguments; support immediate policy revocation.
control.commercialUse: A reusable policy proxy for enterprise agents that need auditable least-privilege access to databases, files and APIs without trusting model compliance.

limitations: This is an offline replay of logged tool calls, not a live patched Riley deployment.
The replay validates deterministic routing decisions, not end-to-end attack success rate or latency.
Observed public operations are not a labeled benign-task benchmark, so no false-positive rate is claimed.
A production implementation should use typed tool schemas or a real SQL AST, not regex parsing.
Gemma 3 27B has not been tested in the available artifacts.

officialCoverage.evidence: Patient attempts blocked; 111 public-reference rows paginated
